title: Gating Experiment Using Affect Bursts
author: Simon Schaerlaeken
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rr2d58e

steps.title: Select emotion recordings
steps.instruction: Choose recordings from the Geneva Multimodal Emotion Portrayals database: 20 recordings each for anger, fear, joy, sadness, and neutral; 10 recordings for disgust (no surprise recordings).

steps.title: Normalize audio and trim silences
steps.instruction: Using Praat version 5.3.51 on Windows, normalize the volume of each recording with a coefficient that balances average and maximum energy, then remove silences at the beginning and end of each file.

steps.title: Segment recordings into chunks
steps.instruction: In Praat 5.3.51 (Windows), cut each normalized recording into consecutive chunks of 50 ms duration.

steps.title: Create stimulus lists
steps.instruction: Generate multiple lists each containing 105 stimuli selected from the full set of chunks; present each list in a pseudo‑random order. Ensure that three or four different participants will evaluate each stimulus, yielding a total of 8 400 stimulus presentations. Designate 72 of the stimuli to be shown 10 times each for reliability testing.

steps.title: Prepare experimental software
steps.instruction: Program the experiment in Windev version 15 (Windows) with a screen resolution of 1280 × 1024 px. Set the default audio output volume to 50 % (participants may adjust it) and provide headphones for all participants.

steps.title: Run participant session
steps.instruction: For each participant, follow this sequence:

substeps.instruction: Obtain written informed consent and collect demographic information.
Display task instructions on the screen.
Present three practice trials using stimuli not included in the main task.
Present the participant‑specific list of 105 stimuli in pseudo‑random order; each stimulus is played once.
After each stimulus, have the participant move sliders (0–100) for anger, fear, joy, sadness, disgust, surprise, and neutral; at least one slider must be moved.
Collect a confidence rating on a continuous scale for each trial.
Allow the participant to adjust volume if needed.
Total session duration should be approximately 30 minutes.

steps.title: Anonymize collected data
steps.instruction: After the session, remove all personally identifying information from the dataset in accordance with the ethics commission’s requirements.

steps.title: Bin stimuli by duration
steps.instruction: Assign each stimulus to duration bins based on the percentage of its total length: a coarse set at 25 % intervals (25 %, 50 %, 75 %, 100 %) and a detailed set at 10 % intervals (10 %, 20 %, …, 100 %). For example, a stimulus derived from a 100 ms original recording that lasts 150 ms belongs to the 25 % bin (coarse) and the 20 % bin (detailed).

steps.title: Compute unbiased hit rate (Hu) per gate
steps.instruction: For every emotion at each 10 % gate, define a trial as a hit when the highest slider value matches the presented emotion. Build a confusion matrix across all participants and calculate the unbiased hit rate (Hu) for each emotion‑gate combination.

steps.title: Compute participant‑level Hu
steps.instruction: Using each participant’s own confusion matrix, calculate Hu for each emotion at the four coarse 25 % gates (25 %, 50 %, 75 %, 100 %). These participant‑specific Hu scores provide variability for subsequent statistical modeling.

steps.title: Linear mixed‑model analysis
steps.instruction: Fit linear mixed models (LMMs) with the lme4 package version 1.1‑17 (Windows). Fixed effects: emotion (anger, sadness, joy, disgust, fear, neutral) and gate duration (25 %, 50 %, 75 %, 100 %). Random intercepts: participant. Use a step‑up strategy to test combinations of fixed effects and chi‑square difference tests for significance. Include the four principal components of acoustic features (see step 14) as additional fixed effects.

steps.title: Polynomial contrast of recognition curves
steps.instruction: For each emotion’s recognition curve (Hu across gates), perform polynomial regression using Phia version 0.2‑1 (Windows) and Matlab R2016b. Record the polynomial coefficients and root‑mean‑square error (RMSE) to assess non‑linear shape.

steps.title: Extract acoustic features
steps.instruction: Using openSMILE (Windows) with the Geneva Minimalist Acoustic Parameter Set (42 features) developed by audEERING, extract the full set of acoustic descriptors for every original recording.

steps.title: Dimensionality reduction via PCA
steps.instruction: Apply a separate principal component analysis (PCA) to the 42 acoustic features for each emotion. Retain the first four components that together explain the cumulative sum of eigenvalues as specified, and use these components as predictors in the LMMs (step 10).
